sectionsUsed: 4.10.4 The label element: the for attribute, if specified, must be the ID of a labelable element; otherwise a label's labeled control is its first labelable descendant (wrapping); activating the label focuses or activates the control; the labels IDL attribute lists a control's labels. Page claims: teach step 2, label fixer, preview read from the labels property, GIFT o1 items.
4.10.5.3.4 The required attribute: a required, mutable control with an empty value is suffering from being missing. Page claims: required in teach step 3, rule builder, apply question.

4.10.5.3.6 The pattern attribute: the pattern is compiled as ^(?:pattern)$ so it must match the entire value; the check runs only if the value is not the empty string; the attribute applies to text, search, url, tel, email and password. Page claims: pattern skips empty values, pattern not on number, GIFT o2 empty and pattern.

4.10.5.3.7 The min and max attributes: underflow and overflow constraints for types with a minimum and maximum (number, date and others); the attributes do not apply to the Text state. Page claims: min and max need a number or date type, apply distractor b, GIFT o2 min on a text field.

4.10.5.1.5 E-mail state and 4.10.5.1.12 Number state: type mismatch for a value that is not a valid email address; number values. Page claims: type email and type number in teach step 3, decoy type email in the rule builder.

4.10.5.3.10 The placeholder attribute: a short hint; the placeholder attribute should not be used as an alternative to a label, because the label is shown at all times. Page claims: a placeholder is not a label, Full name fix, GIFT o1 placeholder only.

4.10.21.2 Constraint validation: on submission the user agent interactively validates the constraints and stops submission if any control is invalid. 4.10.21.3 The constraint validation API: checkValidity() and the ValidityState flags valueMissing, typeMismatch, patternMismatch, rangeUnderflow, rangeOverflow. Page claims: browser blocks invalid submission, rule builder uses checkValidity().

Introduction note: HTML constraint validation does not remove the need for validation on the server side; invalid requests can still be sent by modifying HTML in developer tools, by hand-crafting an HTTP request or programmatically; always validate on the server, consistent with the client. Page claims: prediction, teach step 4, where-checks-run sorter, GIFT o3.
Document conformance requirements: aria-label may be used on button and input elements to provide an accessible name. Page claims: aria-label for an icon-only button.
